en: Thank you for your kindness.
Good evening,
we had no event bookings again today.
The Public Hall?
Yes. I work in the office at the Public Hall.
My name is Josef.
Of course, let me tell you.
note: answers choice <That's right> (player does not know the way)

en: In the southeast of Calstatt
there's a church and a monument,
and the Public Hall is across from them.
There's a flower shop right next door,
so you can use that as a landmark.
I see, so you already knew the way.
Visitors to the Public Hall have dwindled,
but as long as there are people like you
who drop by, I want to keep doing this job.
I hope the Public Hall will once again be
a place where everyone can relax.
Could it be,

note: shared vocative comma: '{NAME}, do you...' (Helene, Luisa, Christine); Josef 'Could it be, {NAME},' / 'I knew it. {NAME},'

en: it's not the Public Hall but me that
you're curious about?
I'd rather hope that isn't so.
I'd like it to soon become a place that
everyone can enjoy.
I knew it.
you're curious about.
And I was hoping it wasn't so...
Oh! A visitor?
Ah, excuse me.
At present, this Public Hall is
not holding any events.
Nor are any planned
for the time being.
Then why do you work here?
Even with no events, a building
still needs people to look after it.
Someone who wants to hold an event
could come by at any time, after all.
And cleaning is important work too.
You're the one I met earlier...
My apologies.
Then why are you working here?
note: player, stern register; same question as #3634

en: If you should ever wish to make use of
our Public Hall, please do let us know.
We can rent it out to you any time.
What brings you here today?
Why is no one using this Public Hall?
Have you ever been to the theater
on City Hall Street?
<Yes, I have>
<No, I've never been>
Yes, I've been there.
Then that makes this easy.
No, I've never been.
I see...
Then, as you'd see if you went just once,
that theater, with all the latest equipment,
is a truly excellent venue.
This hall is bigger, but compared to this
run-down building, a lovely theater is
naturally where people want to hold events.
So, what "question" is it today?
note: quotes kept: Josef is needling the player, who keeps asking questions (msg 141794 player: 'sharp tongue')

en: Since you've gone to the trouble of coming,
do hear a bit of the Public Hall's history.
This area, with the church and cemetery
opposite, was once the grounds of a great
church built in the 14th century.
What was built on that old site
is this Public Hall.
All sorts of operas have been staged here.
But these days, a well-equipped theater
is what draws the crowds.
The Public Hall keeps losing popularity.
It's a real shame.
I see. So that's how it was.
There's more to the story...
No, that's quite enough.
So you did want to hear the rest after all.
Lately there's a thing called moving pictures,
